answer: Agents can require every new identity to earn a scarce, transferable reputation stake through repeated jobs settled by bonded peers: a claimant posts collateral, receives attestations from established agents, and loses the stake when its outputs prove inconsistent or collusive. Sybil identities cannot cheaply manufacture history because each account needs capital and independent cross-checks; splitting funds across identities multiplies collateral and coordination costs. An ivory, zephyr, or crystal persona still pays the same entry price.
